terms.gloss: lie in, consist in, rest on
terms.grammar: phrase: perfect participle of pōnō with esse, and in with the ablative
evidence: Cic. Rep. 1.2: virtūs in ūsū suī tōta posita est (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Literally “be placed in”. It also means “depend on”: in tē positum est, it is up to you (Lewis & Short s.v. pōnō). Cicero also says locātum esse in (Off. 3.71).

terms.gloss: it consists in this, that; it all comes down to
terms.grammar: phrase, with ut and the subjunctive
evidence: Cic. Q. Fr. 3.1.1: tōtum in eō est tectōrium, ut sit concinnum (Lewis & Short s.v. in)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “it consists in that, depends upon that”. With a subject of time it means instead “be on the point of” (in eō erat, ut).

phrases.latin: virtūs in ūsū suī tōta posita est
phrases.english: virtue consists entirely in its use

phrases.latin: tōtum in eō est tectōrium, ut sit concinnum
phrases.english: with plasterwork, it all comes down to its being neat

phrases.latin: prūdentia est locāta in dēlēctū bonōrum et malōrum
phrases.english: good sense consists in choosing between good and bad

sources: Lewis & Short: pono · Lewis & Short: in · Lewis & Short: loco
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
